data.narrative:
Cobod, a Series A-stage housing and construction company founded by Henrik Lund-Nielsen, is evaluated within a narrow comp universe of two identified private peers (Inversion Space and Material Evolution). No public comparables exist in this nascent sector segment, limiting benchmarking depth.

The valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, using Cobod's $46M total raised as a baseline proxy for current enterprise value. A 2.0x step-up multiplier, reflecting typical Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yields an implied valuation of $92M. This single method-driven approach produces a triangulated range of $78M (low) to $106M (high), with $92M as the central estimate.

The median $92M valuation reflects assumed dilution and risk-adjusted return expectations between Series A and Series B or comparable extension rounds. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the two-peer comp set given the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of construction technology; the applicability of a 2.0x multiplier absent stage-specific financing velocity data for this sector; and the absence of revenue, unit economics, or technology differentiation metrics that would typically anchor construction-tech valuations. A fuller analysis would benefit from expanded comps, founder pedigree validation, and unit-level traction data.
